title: Backend comparison, winner wiring, tests and docs
description: Compare backends on held-out accuracy, confusion matrix, throughput, model size, and aggregate-only real-corpus agreement vs VADER; wire the winning ML backend into --sentiment-backend keeping vader as fallback; update tests and docs.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Winner wired: --sentiment-backend transformer now selects the go_emotions-mapped 3-class backend (held-out 0.731, never mislabels neutral, 50.4% agreement with VADER); vader stays the meter default and fallback; comparison candidates remain selectable as transformer-cardiff, transformer-xlmr, transformer-sst2. Real per-source sentiment with the winner (aggregate counts only): 24h 92 scored mean +0.004 (10 pos / 70 neu / 12 neg); today 25 scored mean +0.121 (4/21/0); all-time 3012 scored mean +0.056 (435/2307/270) with per-source claude-code 680 (+0.069), cursor-agent 934 (+0.045), codex 712 (+0.061), grok-bot 240 (+0.056), antigravity 446 (+0.048). Tests: 197 suites, 1612 passing, build clean, lint only the pre-existing packet-validation.spec.ts error. Recommendation: keep vader as the meter default; go_emotions-mapped is the default ML backend; do not install Ollama/llama.cpp for this (1-2 GB runtime, far slower).
